critical_code_review_comments: routes_household.create_invite: reuses ANY pending invite even if it was created for a different email; body.email is only stored, never enforced during join. Acceptable for the invite-code model but worth documenting.

routes_household.remove_member: reassigns the removed user to a fresh household (onboarded=false), but their existing bills/txns/wallets stay in the ex-household. If that user later logs in, ensure_household() creates them a blank household — their historical data is effectively archived under admin. Consider a follow-up flow to copy/split (or at least explicit warning in UI).

routes_bills.pay_bill: no idempotency — clicking Bayar twice quickly on a 'once' bill just re-inserts a duplicate expense and re-decrements the wallet. For 'monthly' it advances the date twice. Add a guard on is_paid_current_cycle or use a debounce on the UI button.

routes_finance._parse_amount: strips commas AND dots unconditionally when count(',')<=1 — 'Rp 12,50' (decimal) will be parsed as 1250, not 12.50. Only Indonesian-style thousand separators are supported; document or normalize.

routes_finance.import_transactions: transfer rows resolve to_wallet via resolve_wallet which auto-creates a cash wallet if missing — silent side effect for typos. Consider requiring existing wallet for transfers or returning a warning row.
Dashboard upcoming_bills filter is computed in Python after fetching ALL unpaid bills; for households with many bills this is O(n). Push the 7-day filter into Mongo as it is done in /bills/upcoming.
MAX_HOUSEHOLD_MEMBERS = 2 hard-coded in models.py — fine for MVP but should live in config/env for future paid tier.
